item.title: Ohio girl’s $768 lemonade stand grows into nonprofit that raises over $5 million for hospitals
item.description: After her time at Cincinnati Children's Hospital, Payton Obert initiated a lemonade stand to assist children in distress. What started as a simple venture has evolved into Payton's Lemonade Stand, amassing over $5 million for various children's charities. The nonprofit not only supplies toys and necessary items to kids facing illness but also encourages community participation, proving that even small gestures can spark tremendous positive impacts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas family has owned a 650-acre Lake Palestine ranch since 1940; a $10 million deal will turn the property into a new state park
item.description: In a strategic move for conservation, a sprawling 650-acre ranch in East Texas is set to transform into a state park. Acquired by the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation from the long-time Pollard family, this land has a rich history dating back to 1940. The park’s development will proceed in stages, initially offering guided access before introducing more facilities for visitors.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Shopper’s C$5 thrift-store painting turns out to be a David Bowie original, sells for C$108,120
item.description: A lucky shopper stumbled upon a remarkable David Bowie painting at a donation center, priced at just C$5. After expert verification, it was revealed to be D Head XLVI from Bowie's iconic Dead Heads series. Shockingly, the artwork was auctioned for an astounding C$108,120, setting a record for Bowie's art. This astonishing find underscores the thrill of discovering hidden gems and the significance of artistic provenance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pakistan kills 5 TTP militants as violence escalates on Afghanistan border
item.description: In a decisive operation, Pakistani security forces eliminated five militants affiliated with Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This mission was executed based on critical intelligence that pinpointed various militant hideouts. Alongside this successful strike, the forces seized a substantial arsenal of weapons and ammunition. This action is a response to the recent surge in violence linked to the TTP, emphasizing the military's ongoing commitment to combatting terrorism in the region.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: In the 1970s, an Italian priest sold 12,000 piranhas to Europe; 55 years later his proceeds have funded 350m bridges and an 800m airstrip
item.description: Giovanni Gallo, an Italian Jesuit priest, moved to Marajó Island in Brazil in the 1970s. He organized the preservation and export of 12,000 piranhas to fund community infrastructure projects. These projects included bridges, a cemetery, a dock, and an airstrip for local residents. Gallo also founded the Museu do Marajó, which showcased local history and archaeology.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 658 unmarked graves found at two remote Australian cemeteries after specialist search
item.description: A groundbreaking project has identified 658 previously unmarked graves at the White Cliffs and Menindee cemeteries in Australia. Utilizing advanced non-invasive scanning techniques, Hunter Geophysics successfully located these burial sites, ensuring no disturbance to the ground. This initiative aims to enhance cemetery management and heritage conservation, with plans for memorialization at White Cliffs for those honored. Such efforts emphasize the crucial need to preserve local history and cemetery documentation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Garland Bel-Air Estate Sale: Judy Garland home sells for $11.1 million; links to Hollywood’s Golden Age
item.description: The historic Bel-Air estate once owned by Judy Garland has been sold for $11.1 million, slightly below its listing price of $11.495 million. Built in 1938 by the renowned architect Wallace Neff, this traditional-style home showcases five bedrooms and seven bathrooms, set amid lush surroundings. Its ties to Garland's rise in Hollywood continue to intrigue potential buyers drawn to its storied past.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: 81 years after British submarine sank Nazi U-boat, Norway faces mercury threat from its wreck
item.description: Norwegian authorities are grappling with a serious mercury contamination issue stemming from the sunken U-864 submarine, which met its fate during World War II. Recent investigations discovered leaking mercury containers, prompting worries about environmental repercussions. The government is now exploring strategies to mitigate this contamination, with sealing the wreck being one of the options under consideration by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries in Norway.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A Florida owner planned 52 homesites on his 625-acre ranch; county agrees to pay $7.8 million to stop development
item.description: In a bid to safeguard a crucial ecological area, Collier County has finalized an agreement to buy Wildflowerz Ranch, preventing any residential construction on its expansive 625 acres. Valued at approximately $7.8 million after two years of negotiations, this acquisition underscores the county's dedication to conservation and wildlife protection. Additionally, the ranch's current cattle operations will remain intact under a lease that lasts until the end of 2027.

item.title: Illinois-Indiana farmer’s 1,500-acre land legacy sells for $22.46 million after his death
item.description: In a recent two-day auction spanning Illinois and Indiana, Philip Rietveld's farmland portfolio captured significant attention, with 23 tracts fetching an impressive $22.46 million. The event attracted 82 bidders from seven states, demonstrating robust competition among local farmers and landowners, with no institutional players participating. A regional group secured one property in Illinois, reflecting the sustained allure of farmland as a strategic investment opportunity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: John Denver guest house gets fixes; buyer sells for $8.2M
item.description: John Denver's former guest house and music studio in Aspen sold for $8.2 million in November 2025. The recent buyer undertook significant renovations, including a modern kitchen and structural improvements. This property spans 5 acres within a gated community and offers stunning views from Aspen to Snowmass. It consists of two structures totaling 2,912 square feet, including a guest house that served as Denver's studio.
